docs.title: RecycleNet-K8s
docs.text: RecycleNet is an end-to-end MLOps system for waste classification (e.g., glass, paper, cardboard, plastic, metal, and trash) using Transfer Learning in PyTorch (MobileNetV3), experiment tracking with MLflow, containerized deployment, and automated CI/CD pipelines.

docs.title: 🚀 Key Features
docs.text:
• Modular Clean Architecture: Strict separation of concerns adhering to SOLID design principles.
  • Transfer Learning: MobileNetV3-Small fine-tuned for high accuracy and minimal latency.
  • Reproducible Pipelines: Deterministic random seed management across Python, NumPy, PyTorch, and CUDA.
  • MLflow Tracking: Automatic logging of hyperparameters, per-epoch metrics, evaluation artifacts, and registered models.
  • Production-Grade Logging: Dual-mode logging (ANSI colorized console locally, structured JSON for Google Cloud Logging).
  • Strict Type Safety: 100% type annotations verified with mypy and linted with ruff.
  • Cloud-Native Kubernetes: Declarative manifests with zero-trust container security, Burstable QoS, and HPA v2 autoscaling.
  • Continuous DevSecOps: GitHub Actions CI with 5 automated gates and CD to Google Cloud Run via keyless OIDC Workload Identity Federation.

docs.title: 📦 Installation & Setup
docs.text:
RecycleNet uses uv for ultra-fast dependency management:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/PilotLeoYan/RecycleNet-K8s.git
cd RecycleNet-K8s

# Install dependencies (including dev and docs groups)
uv sync --all-groups

docs.title: 🏃 Running the Training Pipeline
docs.text:
Execute the end-to-end training pipeline from the command line:

# Run training pipeline
uv run python -m src.main

Launch the local MLflow dashboard to explore metrics and artifacts:

uv run mlflow ui --backend-store-uri sqlite:///mlflow.db

docs.title: 🛡️ DevSecOps & Cloud Deployment
docs.text:
Verify CI quality gates and cloud deployment rules offline:

uv run python -m src.devsecops.orchestrator

docs.title: Architecture & MLOps Lifecycle
docs.text: RecycleNet follows a four-phase MLOps roadmap designed for robust, reproducible, and scalable production deployments.

docs.title: 📐 SOLID Principles in RecycleNet
docs.text: Principle Implementation in RecycleNet S - Single Responsibility Components are decoupled: DataIngestion extracts datasets, DataTransformation generates tensor pipelines, ModelTrainer executes optimization loops, and LogModel interacts with MLflow. O - Open/Closed Training pipelines and architectures are extensible without modifying existing orchestration logic. L - Liskov Substitution Custom dataset transformations and model wrappers seamlessly adhere to standard PyTorch interfaces (Dataset, DataLoader, nn.Module). I - Interface Segregation Fine-grained interfaces for metric calculation, data loading, and tracking rather than monolithic classes. D - Dependency Inversion High-level orchestrators (TrainPipeline) receive configurations and abstractions via dependency injection rather than hardcoded global values.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & DevSecOps Philosophy
docs.text:
In enterprise MLOps architectures, developing high-performing computer vision models and local containerized endpoints represents only the first milestone of the product lifecycle. To achieve reliable production maturity, systems must embed DevSecOps practices—shifting quality assurance, security auditing, and cloud governance left into automated pipelines.

RecycleNet-K8s Phase 4 establishes an automated, zero-trust Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) foundation targeting Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The architecture guarantees:

  • Automated Quality & Security Gates: Every pull request is verified against strict code formatting, comprehensive type checking, AST-based security vulnerability analysis, and enforced test coverage thresholds.
  • Keyless Cloud Authentication: Zero static JSON service account keys. Authentication between GitHub Actions and GCP is handled entirely through short-lived cryptographic tokens via OpenID Connect (OIDC) and Workload Identity Federation.
  • Immutable Container Artifacts: Container builds are uniquely and immutably tagged with commit SHA identifiers (sha-${{ github.sha }}) in Google Artifact Registry (GAR), eliminating configuration drift and enabling deterministic rollbacks.
  • Serverless Cloud Run Deployment: Production inference workloads deploy serverlessly to Google Cloud Run with managed TLS, granular resource limits (1Gi RAM, 1 CPU), and dynamic auto-scaling from 1 warm instance up to 5 instances under load.
  • Local Simulation & Offline Verification: A dedicated orchestration CLI validates workflow schemas, security constraints, and deployment scenarios offline without incurring cloud egress costs.

docs.title: 2. End-to-End DevSecOps Architecture & Pipeline Topology
docs.text:
The continuous lifecycle is split into two specialized GitHub Actions workflows:

  1. Continuous Integration (.github/workflows/ci.yaml / ci.yml): Runs on every pull request and push to main to validate quality, security, and functional correctness.
  2. Continuous Deployment (.github/workflows/cd.yaml): Runs automatically upon merging to main, executing keyless GCP federation, container compilation, image registry push, and Cloud Run service rollout.

docs.title: CI Pipeline Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Trigger(["Git Push / Pull Request"]) --> Checkout["1. Checkout Repository<br/>actions/checkout@v4"]
    Checkout --> SetupUV["2. Setup Python Toolchain<br/>astral-sh/setup-uv"]
    SetupUV --> InstallDeps["3. Deterministic Sync<br/>uv sync --frozen --all-groups"]

    subgraph QualityGates["5 Strict Quality & Security Gates"]
        InstallDeps --> RuffFmt["Gate 1: Format Check<br/>ruff format --check ."]
        RuffFmt --> RuffLint["Gate 2: Linter Inspection<br/>ruff check ."]
        RuffLint --> Mypy["Gate 3: Strict Typing<br/>mypy ."]
        Mypy --> Bandit["Gate 4: Security AST Scan<br/>bandit -r src/"]
        Bandit --> Pytest["Gate 5: Pytest & Coverage<br/>pytest --cov=src --cov-fail-under=80"]
    end

    Pytest --> Success(["CI Status: PASSED ✅<br/>Ready for Peer Review / Merge"])

docs.text:

    MergeMain(["Merge Commit to 'main'"]) --> CIValidation{"CI Quality Gates<br/>Passed?"}

    CIValidation -- Yes --> OIDCAuth["1. Keyless GCP OIDC Auth<br/>google-github-actions/auth<br/>Workload Identity Federation"]

    DeployCloudRun --> HealthCheck{"7. Cloud Run Startup<br/>& Readiness Probe"}
    HealthCheck -- Healthy --> LiveProduction(["Live Production Endpoint 🚀<br/>Zero-Downtime Traffic Migration"])

docs.title: 3. The 5 CI Quality & Security Gates in Detail
docs.text:
To ensure code stability, prevent regression, and enforce clean architecture, the CI pipeline executes five sequential verification gates:

flowchart LR
    G1["1. astral-sh/setup-uv<br/>Instant Cached Toolchain"] --> G2["2. Ruff Format & Lint<br/>PEP 8 & Clean Code"]
    G2 --> G3["3. Mypy Strict<br/>100% Static Types"]
    G3 --> G4["4. Bandit AST<br/>Security Analysis"]
    G4 --> G5["5. Pytest Coverage<br/>≥ 80% Threshold"]

docs.title: Gate 1: Astral-sh Setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)
docs.text:
• Role: High-performance dependency resolution and virtual environment bootstrapping.
  • Mechanism: Powered by Rust, uv installs and synchronizes dependencies in milliseconds. The workflow caches wheel artifacts using cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock".
  • Command: 
    uv sync --frozen --all-groups --extra cpu
  • Benefit: Guarantees bitwise reproducibility across local development workstations and remote GitHub Actions runners.

docs.title: Gate 2: Ruff Code Formatting & Linting (ruff)
docs.text:
• Role: Comprehensive syntax verification, import classification, and PEP 8 formatting.
  • Configuration: Adheres to strict 88-character line length (line-length = 88), Py314 target conventions, and import sorting (select = ["E", "F", "I", "W", "UP"]).
  • Commands: 
    uv run ruff format --check .
uv run ruff check .
  • Benefit: Eliminates stylistic discrepancies and enforces idiomatic Python patterns before code review.

docs.title: Gate 3: Mypy Strict Static Type Verification (mypy)
docs.text:
• Role: Compile-time validation of types across domain models, configuration schemas, and pipeline components.
  • Configuration: Flags untyped function definitions (disallow_untyped_defs = true), warns on unreachable branches (warn_unreachable = true), and prohibits arbitrary dynamic typing.
  • Command: 
    uv run mypy .
  • Benefit: Prevents insidious runtime crashes such as AttributeError or TypeError before code reaches containerization.

docs.title: Gate 4: Bandit AST Security Analysis (bandit)
docs.text:
• Role: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) analyzing Python Abstract Syntax Trees (AST).
  • Configuration: Defined in pyproject.toml, scanning src/ while ignoring false-positive assertion checks (B101) and pseudo-random generators in non-cryptographic ML trials (B311).
  • Command: 
    uv run bandit -r src/ -c pyproject.toml
  • Benefit: Proactively discovers high-risk vulnerabilities including hardcoded secrets, shell injection vulnerabilities, unsafe deserialization, and improper socket bindings.

docs.title: Gate 5: Pytest Unit & Integration Coverage (pytest-cov)
docs.text:
• Role: Functional correctness verification across data ingestion, model building, ONNX export, REST API endpoints, and Kubernetes orchestration logic.
  • Enforcement: Enforces an explicit 80%+ coverage threshold (fail_under = 80). If test coverage drops below 80%, the CI pipeline immediately fails, blocking PR merge.
  • Command: 
    uv run pytest tests/ -v --durations=10 --cov=src --cov-fail-under=80
  • Benefit: Assures that all critical algorithmic logic, edge-case exception handling, and API serialization paths are validated against regressions.

docs.title: 4. Keyless Workload Identity Federation (GitHub Actions ↔ GCP OIDC)
docs.text:
Traditional CI/CD setups rely on long-lived Service Account JSON keys stored in repository secrets. This represents a significant security liability: - Keys do not automatically expire. - Keys are susceptible to leakage or insider exfiltration. - Secret rotation requires manual effort and risk of downtime.

RecycleNet adopts OpenID Connect (OIDC) and Google Cloud Workload Identity Federation, establishing a cryptographic trust exchange between GitHub's OIDC Provider and GCP Security Token Service (STS).

docs.title: Keyless Token Exchange Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant GHA as GitHub Actions Runner
    participant GH_OIDC as GitHub OIDC Provider<br/>(token.actions.githubusercontent.com)
    participant GCP_STS as GCP Security Token Service<br/>(sts.googleapis.com)
    participant GCP_IAM as GCP IAM Service Account<br/>(github-deployer@...)
    participant GCP_SVC as Google Cloud Services<br/>(Artifact Registry & Cloud Run)

    GHA->>GH_OIDC: Request OIDC JWT Token (audience: gcp-wip)
    GH_OIDC-->>GHA: Signed OIDC JWT Token
    GHA->>GCP_STS: Exchange Token (AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity)
    Note over GCP_STS: Validates JWT signature,<br/>issuer & repo claim assertions<br/>(e.g. repository == 'PilotLeoYan/RecycleNet-K8s')
    GCP_STS-->>GHA: Short-lived Federated GCP Access Token
    GHA->>GCP_IAM: Impersonate Service Account
    Note over GCP_IAM: Verifies roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser<br/>permission binding
    GCP_IAM-->>GHA: Short-lived OAuth2 Access Token (valid for 1 hour)
    GHA->>GCP_SVC: Authenticated Deployment Requests<br/>(Push Docker image to GAR & update Cloud Run)
    GCP_SVC-->>GHA: Deployment Succeeded (HTTP 200 OK)

docs.title: GitHub Actions OIDC Configuration
docs.text:
In .github/workflows/cd.yaml, permissions require id-token: write to issue OIDC credentials:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

steps:
  - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud via OIDC
    uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
    with:
      workload_identity_provider: "projects/1234567890/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions-pool/providers/github-provider"
      service_account: "github-deployer@recyclenet-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
      token_format: "access_token"

docs.title: 5. Immutable Container Versioning with Google Artifact Registry (GAR)
docs.text: To maintain a secure software supply chain, all container artifacts produced by the CD pipeline are published to Google Artifact Registry (GAR).

docs.title: Tagging Convention & Traceability
docs.text:
Using mutable tags such as :latest in production environments introduces substantial risk: - It obscures which Git commit generated the running image. - Rollbacks are non-deterministic because the tag points to different image digests over time. - Multi-container clusters may run heterogeneous revisions under the same tag.

RecycleNet enforces immutable commit SHA tagging:

$$\text{Image Identifier} = \text{GAR_LOCATION-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/REPOSITORY/recyclenet-api:sha-}\${ \text{GITHUB_SHA} }$$

# Tagging with full Git commit SHA
docker build -t us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/recyclenet-prod/recyclenet-registry/recyclenet-api:sha-${{ github.sha }} .
docker push us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/recyclenet-prod/recyclenet-registry/recyclenet-api:sha-${{ github.sha }}

Every deployed container image can be audited directly back to its exact Git commit, author, test logs, and PR approval.

docs.title: 6. Serverless Deployment: Google Cloud Run vs GKE
docs.text: RecycleNet supports dual production deployment targets: Google Cloud Run (managed serverless) and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) (declarative cluster).

docs.title: Comparative Architecture Analysis
docs.text: Architectural Criterion Google Cloud Run (Serverless) Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Compute Paradigm Managed serverless container execution Managed Kubernetes cluster (nodes/pods) Operational Overhead Near zero (no nodes, OS updates, or control plane) Moderate to high (cluster upgrades, daemonsets, CNI) Autoscaling Mechanics Sub-second request-driven container scaling HPA + Cluster Autoscaler (node provisioning latency) Idle Cost Zero (scales to zero when traffic stops) Fixed baseline costs for control plane and node pool Ingress & Networking Managed HTTPS, automatic TLS certificates, DDoS mitigation Requires Ingress controller (NGINX), Cert-Manager, DNS Ideal Workload Profile REST inference APIs, intermittent or spiky demand High-throughput distributed pipelines, GPU training

docs.title: Cloud Run Production Deployment Parameters
docs.text:
For Phase 4 serverless inference, the CD pipeline deploys the container with strict resource boundaries:

gcloud run deploy recyclenet-api \
  --image="us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/recyclenet-prod/recyclenet-registry/recyclenet-api:sha-${{ github.sha }}" \
  --region="us-central1" \
  --platform="managed" \
  --port=8000 \
  --memory=1Gi \
  --cpu=1 \
  --min-instances=1 \
  --max-instances=5 \
  --concurrency=80 \
  --allow-unauthenticated

docs.title: Parameter Rationale:
docs.text:
• --port=8000: Matches the internal FastAPI port exposed in the multi-stage Dockerfile.
  • --memory=1Gi: Provides ample headroom for loading ONNX Runtime CPU inference engines and PyTorch image transforms without triggering out-of-memory errors.
  • --cpu=1: Allocates a dedicated virtual CPU core, providing deterministic request latency.
  • --min-instances=1: Keeps one warm instance active 24/7 to completely eliminate cold-start latency for interactive users.
  • --max-instances=5: Sets a strict upper boundary to prevent runaway cloud bills during unexpected denial-of-service or load spikes.
  • --concurrency=80: Allows up to 80 simultaneous requests per container instance before provisioning additional replicas.

docs.title: 7. Offline DevSecOps Validation & Simulation CLI
docs.text:
To facilitate verification of DevSecOps pipelines and deployment specifications on air-gapped development machines without active GCP access, RecycleNet provides an offline simulation CLI:

uv run python -m src.devsecops.orchestrator

docs.title: Available CLI Options
docs.text:
Options:
  --help          Show help message and exit
  --ci-only       Execute only CI quality gate rule validation
  --cd-only       Execute only CD GCP OIDC and deployment rule validation
  --format-md     Export execution summary as GitHub Flavored Markdown

docs.title: Verification Capabilities
docs.text:
• Static Workflow Linting: Parses .github/workflows/ci.yaml and .github/workflows/cd.yaml to ensure all 5 quality gates and OIDC actions are configured correctly.
  • OIDC Claims Simulation: Simulates the STS cryptographic token exchange, verifying subject claim restrictions (repo:PilotLeoYan/RecycleNet-K8s:ref:refs/heads/main).
  • Cloud Run Scaling Trajectory: Computes instance scaling trajectories across simulated request traffic patterns, verifying min/max boundaries and concurrency quotas.

docs.title: 8. Supply Chain Security, CVE Version Patches & CodeQL CWE-020 Hardening
docs.text: Beyond runtime container hardening, Phase 4 enforces proactive software supply chain security across both transitive Python dependencies (pyproject.toml and uv.lock) and static application security testing (GitHub Advanced Security / CodeQL).

docs.title: 8.1 Transitive Dependency CVE Remediation ([tool.uv] override-dependencies)
docs.text:
To eliminate vulnerabilities introduced by upstream transitive dependencies (such as MLflow, GitPython, and OpenTelemetry), pyproject.toml pins hardened floor versions via [tool.uv] override-dependencies and locks their SHA-256 digests in uv.lock:

[tool.uv]
package = false
override-dependencies = [
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    "gitpython>=3.2.1",
    "graphql-core>=3.2.12",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.45.1",
]
Package Previous Version Patched Version (uv.lock) Override Constraint Severity & Vulnerability Remediated gitpython 3.1.62 3.2.1 >=3.2.1 High (Dependabot #26): Remote Code Execution (RCE) where submodule .git paths were validated only after cloning into untrusted repositories. graphql-core 3.2.11 3.2.13 >=3.2.12 High (Dependabot #24 & #25): Denial of Service (DoS) via comment tokens bypassing max_tokens parser limits and quadratic complexity in OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged validation. opentelemetry-api 1.44.0 1.45.1 >=1.45.1 Moderate (Dependabot #23): Unbounded tracestate W3C header parsing resulting in CPU/memory exhaustion (opentelemetry-sdk & opentelemetry-proto upgraded in lockstep to 1.45.1). cryptography <50.0.0 >=50.0.0 >=50.0.0 High: Enforces modern OpenSSL bindings and X.509 certificate verification primitives.

docs.title: 8.2 CodeQL SAST Hardening (CWE-020: Incomplete URL Substring Sanitization)
docs.text:
During automated CodeQL analysis (py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization), naive substring or prefix checks on URLs and domains are vulnerable to subdomain/suffix spoofing (e.g., https://iam.googleapis.com.attacker.com/projects/123 or deployer@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com.attacker.com).

In src/devsecops/orchestrator.py (GcpOidcWorkloadIdentitySimulator.validate_claims), OIDC claim verification is hardened using RFC-compliant URL parsing (urllib.parse.urlparse) and exact domain label matching:

  1. OIDC Audience (aud) Verification:
  2. Parses audience with urllib.parse.urlparse(audience).
  3. Enforces exact equality on parsed_audience.scheme == "https" and parsed_audience.hostname == "iam.googleapis.com", combined with path prefix /projects/.
  4. GCP IAM Service Account (service_account) Verification:
  5. Partitions the email identifier via sa.partition("@") and rejects embedded path/scheme characters (/ or :).
  6. Splits the domain into labels and verifies the exact 4-label GCP IAM structure: <project-id>.iam.gserviceaccount.com (sa_domain_parts[1:] == ["iam", "gserviceaccount", "com"]).
  7. Regression Testing:
  8. Verified via spoofed-domain unit tests in tests/test_devsecops_orchestrator.py.

docs.title: 🚀 GCP Cloud Run Deployment Guide — Zero-Cost Serverless Inference
docs.text: This guide explains how to deploy the RecycleNet-K8s inference service on Google Cloud Run with a $0.00 zero-cost profile, ideal for live demos, technical evaluations, and staging environments.

docs.title: 🎯 1.1. What is Google Cloud Run?
docs.text: Google Cloud Run is a serverless, fully managed container platform from Google Cloud. Unlike traditional Kubernetes clusters (GKE) or virtual machines (Compute Engine) that charge by the hour regardless of traffic, Cloud Run bills exclusively for CPU and memory consumed while actively processing HTTP requests.

docs.title: 💡 1.2. Why Cloud Run instead of GKE for a demo?
docs.text:
1. Per-millisecond billing: When no requests arrive the container scales down to zero — idle cost = $0.00.
  2. GCP permanent free tier (monthly):
  3. 2,000,000 HTTP requests free.
  4. 360,000 GB-seconds of memory free.
  5. 180,000 vCPU-seconds of compute free.
  6. 1 GiB outbound traffic to North America free.
  7. Real demo consumption (~3–10 users, one inference each):
  8. Average inference time: $\approx 250\,\text{ms}$.
  9. Total vCPU usage: $10 \times 0.25\,\text{s} = 2.5\,\text{vCPU-s}$ (of 180,000 free).
  10. Total RAM usage: $10 \times 0.25\,\text{s} = 2.5\,\text{GB-s}$ (of 360,000 free).
  11. Effective charge: $0.00 USD.

docs.title: 🛡️ 1.3. The Two Wallet-Protection Flags
docs.text:
Every deployment enforces:

Flag Value Effect --min-instances 0 Scale-to-zero when idle; no charge at rest. --max-instances 2 Hard cap; prevents runaway billing spikes.

docs.title: 2. 📋 GCP Project Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Parameter Value Project Name RecycleNet-K8s Project ID recyclenet-k8s Recommended Region us-central1 (full free tier) Cloud Run Service recyclenet-service Artifact Registry recyclenet-images Application Port 8000 (FastAPI / Uvicorn ASGI)

[!NOTE] The live service URL takes the form https://recyclenet-service-<hash>-uc.a.run.app and is printed at the end of the deploy script. It changes whenever the Cloud Run service is deleted and re-created.

docs.title: 3. 🛠️ Quick Automated Deployment (One Command)
docs.text: The repository ships a fully automated script at scripts/deploy_gcp.sh.

docs.title: Step 1 — Authenticate gcloud
docs.text:
gcloud auth login

A browser window will open to complete Google account authorisation.

docs.title: Step 2 — Run the deployment
docs.text:
./scripts/deploy_gcp.sh
# or
make deploy-gcp

The script automatically:

  1. Resolves gcloud and docker-credential-gcloud in PATH.
  2. Verifies the active authenticated account.
  3. Sets the active project (recyclenet-k8s).
  4. Enables run.googleapis.com and artifactregistry.googleapis.com.
  5. Creates the recyclenet-images Docker repository in Artifact Registry.
  6. Configures the Docker credential helper for the regional registry.
  7. Builds (or reuses) the local recyclenet-api:demo image.
  8. Tags and pushes the image to Artifact Registry.
  9. Deploys to Cloud Run with --min-instances=0 and --allow-unauthenticated.
  10. Verifies the live /health endpoint and prints the public URL.

[!IMPORTANT] On a first run, Step 3 waits a few seconds after enabling the Artifact Registry API for GCP IAM propagation before querying the API. The script handles this automatically with --quiet flags and does not block indefinitely.

docs.title: 4. 🔬 Manual Step-by-Step Deployment
docs.text: If you want to understand or reproduce every command individually:

docs.title: Step 1 — Set the active project
docs.text: gcloud config set project recyclenet-k8s

docs.title: Step 2 — Enable required GCP APIs
docs.text: gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com

docs.title: Step 3 — Create the Artifact Registry Docker repository
docs.text:
gcloud artifacts repositories create recyclenet-images \
    --repository-format=docker \
    --location=us-central1 \
    --description="RecycleNet Docker container images"

docs.title: Step 4 — Configure Docker authentication
docs.text: gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev --quiet

docs.title: Step 5 — Build and tag the Docker image
docs.text:
docker build -t recyclenet-api:demo .

docker tag recyclenet-api:demo \
    us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/recyclenet-k8s/recyclenet-images/recyclenet-api:demo

docs.title: Step 6 — Push to Artifact Registry
docs.text: docker push us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/recyclenet-k8s/recyclenet-images/recyclenet-api:demo

docs.title: Step 7 — Deploy to Cloud Run (zero-cost constraints)
docs.text:
gcloud run deploy recyclenet-service \
    --image="us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/recyclenet-k8s/recyclenet-images/recyclenet-api:demo" \
    --region="us-central1" \
    --platform="managed" \
    --port=8000 \
    --memory=1Gi \
    --cpu=1 \
    --min-instances=0 \
    --max-instances=2 \
    --concurrency=80 \
    --allow-unauthenticated

At completion, gcloud prints the public HTTPS URL.

docs.title: 🌐 Option A — Swagger UI (recommended for demos)
docs.text:
Open in any browser:

https://<YOUR-SERVICE-URL>/docs
  1. Expand POST /predict/.
  2. Click "Try it out".
  3. Upload a waste photo (cardboard, glass, metal, paper, plastic, or trash).

docs.title: ☸️ RecycleNet-K8s: Cloud-Native Orchestration with Local Kubernetes
1. Executive Summary & Orchestration Philosophy
docs.text:
In modern production Machine Learning systems, delivering high inference performance on a single machine is only half the battle. Real-world systems must guarantee high availability (HA), fault tolerance, predictable latency under burst load, and zero-downtime rolling updates.

Derived from Google's internal cluster management system (Borg), Kubernetes (K8s) has emerged as the global standard for cloud-native workload orchestration. RecycleNet-K8s designs and validates a complete, production-grade Kubernetes deployment architecture that can be executed locally with zero cloud costs using Minikube or Kind.

docs.title: Key Engineering Objectives
docs.text:
• High Availability & Redundancy: Decoupled multi-tier deployment (Python FastAPI baseline and Rust Axum high-performance edge tier) running at a baseline of 2 replicas each with Pod Anti-Affinity.
  • Zero-Trust Security: Containers execute under unprivileged non-root users (appuser, UID 10001), drop all Linux kernel capabilities (drop: [ALL]), and prohibit privilege escalation.
  • Resource Governance & QoS: Rigorous CPU and Memory requests and limits configured to guarantee a Burstable Quality of Service (QoS) class, preventing catastrophic OOMKilled (Exit Code 137) crashes.
  • Deterministic Traffic Gating: Decoupled Liveness (/healthz) and Readiness (/ready) probes ensure traffic is never routed to uninitialized model weights, while zero-downtime rolling updates (maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0) guarantee uninterrupted service.
  • Dynamic Autoscaling (HPA v2): Closed-loop Horizontal Pod Autoscaler targeting 70% CPU utilization, scaling from 2 to 5 replicas with aggressive scale-up burst absorption and conservative cooldown stabilization against pod thrashing.

docs.title: 4. Resource Governance, QoS Classes, and OOMKilled Prevention
docs.text: In deep learning serving, memory and CPU allocation is critical. If a container exceeds its memory limits, the Linux kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer terminates the process instantly with Exit Code 137 (SIGKILL).

docs.title: Linux cgroups v2 Governance Mechanics
docs.text:
• CPU Requests: Configured via CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler) shares (cpu.weight). Kubernetes guarantees this proportion of CPU time to the pod under node contention.
  • CPU Limits: Enforced via CFS bandwidth quotas (cpu.cfs_quota_us / cpu.cfs_period_us). If a pod exceeds this limit, its threads are throttled but the container is not killed.
  • Memory Requests: Used by kube-scheduler to place pods on nodes with sufficient unreserved RAM (memory.min / memory.low).
  • Memory Limits: Hard memory ceiling (memory.max). When total RSS + page cache exceeds this value, the kernel triggers an immediate OOM kill event.

docs.title: Quality of Service (QoS) Classification
docs.text:
Kubernetes assigns one of three QoS classes based on resource definitions: 1. Guaranteed: requests == limits for all CPU and memory resources. 2. Burstable: requests < limits, allowing pods to utilize spare node capacity during traffic bursts while maintaining strict guarantees. 3. BestEffort: No requests or limits specified (highest risk of being evicted under memory pressure).

RecycleNet-K8s configures Burstable QoS for both services, ensuring efficient cluster bin-packing while safeguarding against node starvation:

Workload Dimension Python API (recyclenet-deployment) Rust API (recyclenet-rust-deployment) QoS Class Burstable Burstable CPU Request 250m (0.25 core) 100m (0.1 core) CPU Limit 1000m (1.0 core) 500m (0.5 core) Memory Request 512Mi 64Mi Memory Limit 1Gi (1024Mi) 128Mi OOM Headroom 100% burst buffer (512Mi $\to$ 1Gi) 100% burst buffer (64Mi $\to$ 128Mi) High Availability Anti-Affinity Soft (preferredDuringScheduling) Soft (preferredDuringScheduling)

docs.text:

    participant Pod as Pod (Container)

    participant Client as External Ingress Traffic

    Note over Pod: Container starting up...
    Kubelet->>Pod: GET /healthz (Liveness Probe)
    Pod-->>Kubelet: 200 OK (Process is alive)

    Kubelet->>Pod: GET /ready (Readiness Probe)

  • Liveness Probe (/healthz): Verifies the event loop (Uvicorn or Tokio) is responsive. If an unhandled deadlock occurs, kubelet restarts the container after failureThreshold: 3.
  • Readiness Probe (/ready): Verifies the deep learning model weights and ONNX session are resident in RAM. Traffic is routed to the pod only after this probe returns 200 OK.

docs.title: Zero-Downtime Rolling Update Strategy
docs.text:
Upgrading model versions or application logic must never disrupt client requests:

strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 0
  • maxSurge: 1: During an update, Kubernetes starts 1 new pod (reaching 3 temporary pods) before terminating any old ones.
  • maxUnavailable: 0: Guarantees that at least 2 healthy pods are actively answering traffic at every millisecond during the deployment rollout.

docs.title: 6. Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA v2) & Control Loop Dynamics
docs.text:
The HorizontalPodAutoscaler (autoscaling/v2) continuously reconciles desired replica counts against actual resource consumption gathered by the metrics-server.

flowchart LR
    M["metrics-server<br/>cAdvisor Scraper"] -->|Current CPU %| C{"HPA Control Loop<br/>T = 15s"}
    C -->|Formula Replicas| S["Scale Controller<br/>scaleTargetRef"]
    S -->|Patch spec.replicas| D["Deployment<br/>recyclenet-deployment"]

docs.title: Mathematical Control Loop Formula
docs.text:
The Kubernetes HPA controller evaluates replica demand using the standard formula:

$$\text{desiredReplicas} = \left\lceil \text{currentReplicas} \times \left( \frac{\text{currentMetricValue}}{\text{desiredMetricValue}} \right) \right\rceil$$

For example, when 2 replicas run at 140% CPU (due to a burst of image classification requests) against the target of 70%:

$$\text{desiredReplicas} = \left\lceil 2 \times \left( \frac{140}{70} \right) \right\rceil = \lceil 2 \times 2 \rceil = 4 \text{ replicas}$$

docs.title: Stabilization Windows & Anti-Flapping Policies
docs.text:
To prevent "pod flapping" (rapid scale-up followed immediately by destructive scale-down):

behavior:
  scaleUp:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
    selectPolicy: Max
    policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 100
        periodSeconds: 15
      - type: Pods
        value: 2
        periodSeconds: 15
  scaleDown:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60
    selectPolicy: Min
    policies:
      - type: Pods
        value: 1
        periodSeconds: 30
  1. Scale-Up (stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0): Immediate response. Upon detecting load, the controller scales up immediately (doubling capacity or adding 2 pods every 15 seconds) to prevent tail latency degradation.
  2. Scale-Down (stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60): Conservative cooldown. The autoscaler inspects the peak metric over the past 60 seconds before removing any pod, shedding only 1 replica every 30 seconds.

kubectl port-forward svc/recyclenet-service 8000:8000 8080:8080

In your main terminal, launch the k6 stress test script targeting the Python endpoint:

k6 run -e TARGET_URL=http://localhost:8000 benchmarks/k6_load_test.js

While k6 ramps up virtual users (from 10 to 60 VUs), watch the HPA controller scale pods in real time:

kubectl get hpa recyclenet-hpa -w

In another terminal, observe new pods being scheduled:

kubectl get pods -l app=recyclenet -w

Observed Scaling Lifecycle: 1. Initial Idle: 2 replicas, CPU usage at 1% / 70%. 2. Stress Ramp-Up: CPU jumps to 125% / 70%. HPA calculates desiredReplicas = 4. 3. Scale-Up Event: Deployment scales from 2 to 4 pods within 15 seconds. 4. Peak Load: CPU hits 160% / 70%. Deployment reaches max capacity: 5 pods. 5. Cooldown Phase: k6 finishes. CPU drops to 0% / 70%. 6. Stabilized Scale-Down: After the 60-second stabilization window, the controller gradually scales down back to 2 replicas (1 replica every 30 seconds).

docs.title: 🏗️ RecycleNet-K8s: Dual Inference & Edge/IoT Serving Architecture
1. Executive Summary & Purpose
docs.text:
The RecycleNet-K8s serving infrastructure is engineered to solve a fundamental dilemma in modern production Machine Learning: how to bridge rapid cloud development with ultra-low latency, deterministic edge inference.

Standard deep learning deployment pipelines frequently rely solely on high-level Python web frameworks (such as FastAPI, Flask, or TorchServe). While well-suited for experimentation and standard cloud APIs, Python introduces considerable drawbacks for edge environments: - High container footprints (~1.2 GB image size due to PyTorch wheels, CUDA dependencies, and Python runtimes). - Significant resident memory consumption (~350–500 MB RSS at idle, scaling up under load). - Non-deterministic tail latency caused by Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) contention and unpredictable Garbage Collection (GC) pauses. - Prolonged cold-start times (2–5 seconds), hindering agile Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA).

To address these challenges, RecycleNet-K8s establishes a Dual Serving Topology: 1. Python Cloud Baseline Tier (src/api/): Built on FastAPI and ONNX Runtime CPU Execution Provider. Provides rapid iteration, dynamic telemetry parsing, and frictionless integration with the MLflow model registry. 2. Rust High-Performance Edge Tier (rust_inference/): Built on Axum 0.8, Tokio, and the ort crate (ONNX Runtime C-API FFI bindings). Delivers sub-millisecond dispatch, zero-copy memory transfers, deterministic execution without garbage collection, a microscopic container footprint (<40 MB), and tiny memory consumption (<45 MB RSS).

Both engines strictly implement identical REST API contracts, guarantee numerical parity, and undergo automated load validation with k6 and a dedicated Python scientific benchmarking harness.

docs.title: 3. SOLID Design of Python Serving Tier (src/api/)
docs.text:
The Python API tier is strictly structured according to the five SOLID principles of software architecture:

classDiagram
    class InferenceModelProtocol {
        <<Protocol / Interface>>
        +__call__(x: Tensor) Tensor
    }
    class OnnxModelWrapper {
        -session: ort.InferenceSession
        -input_name: str
        -output_name: str
        +__call__(x: Tensor | ndarray) Tensor
        +eval() None
    }
    class ImagePreprocessor {
        -transform: v2.Compose
        +preprocess(image_bytes: bytes) Tensor
    }
    class TelemetryParser {
        +parse(telemetry, latitude, longitude) Telemetry
    }
    class InferenceService {
        -preprocessor: ImagePreprocessor
        -telemetry_parser: TelemetryParser
        +predict(model, idx_to_class, image_bytes, ...) PredictionResponse
        +get_info(app_state) InfoResponse
    }

    InferenceModelProtocol <|.. OnnxModelWrapper : Implements
    InferenceService --> InferenceModelProtocol : Uses (Dependency Inversion)
    InferenceService --> ImagePreprocessor : Uses (Single Responsibility)
    InferenceService --> TelemetryParser : Uses (Single Responsibility)
  1. Single Responsibility Principle (SRP):
  2. ImagePreprocessor: Dedicated solely to decoding image bytes, resizing, and normalizing tensors.
  3. TelemetryParser: Dedicated solely to parsing, sanitizing, and validating geographic coordinates.
  4. InferenceService: Coordinates the domain pipeline (preprocessing, inference dispatch, softmax probability mapping).
  5. routes/health.py & routes/predict.py: Focused entirely on HTTP transport, status codes, and routing.
  6. Open/Closed Principle (OCP):
  7. The serving tier can accept any model backend implementing InferenceModelProtocol without altering existing route or service code.
  8. Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP):
  9. OnnxModelWrapper can seamlessly replace a native PyTorch torch.nn.Module. Both accept input tensors and return raw logits.
  10. Interface Segregation Principle (ISP):
  11. InferenceModelProtocol requires only a callable contract __call__(x: Tensor) -> Tensor. Consumers do not depend on heavyweight training or backward-pass methods.
  12. Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP):
  13. InferenceService and route handlers depend upon the abstract InferenceModelProtocol, not concrete ONNX or PyTorch classes. The model instance is injected into app.state during application lifespan.

docs.title: Lifespan State Management
docs.text: Application startup and teardown are managed through FastAPI's @asynccontextmanager lifespan: - Startup: Resolves models/recyclenet.onnx, initializes an ort.InferenceSession with optimized thread configurations (inter_op_num_threads=2, intra_op_num_threads=2), loads label mappings, and sets app.state.model_ready = True. - Teardown: Gracefully deallocates session resources, sets model_ready = False, and releases memory.

docs.title: 4. Systems Programming Architecture: Rust Axum Engine (rust_inference/)
docs.text: The Rust microservice delivers a cloud-native, high-throughput drop-in replacement for the Python API:

docs.title: Architecture Highlights
docs.text:
• Axum Web Framework: Utilizes Axum's modular routing and extractors (Multipart, Json, FormPayload), matching FastAPI's parameter handling.
  • InferenceBackend Trait: Thread-safe abstraction (Send + Sync) encapsulated in Arc<dyn InferenceBackend>: 
    pub trait InferenceBackend: Send + Sync {
    fn predict(&self, image_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<PredictionResult, EngineError>;
    fn run_tensor(&self, tensor: &Array4<f32>) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<f32>), EngineError>;
    fn is_ready(&self) -> bool;
    fn classes(&self) -> &[String];
    fn model_path(&self) -> &Path;
}
  • Zero-Copy Tensor Memory Pipeline:
  • The raw HTTP request bytes are parsed into memory.
  • image::load_from_memory decodes the JPEG/PNG into a pixel buffer.
  • imageops::resize transforms dimensions to $224 \times 224$ via Bilinear interpolation.
  • Normalized floating-point values are written directly into a contiguous 4D ndarray::Array4<f32> buffer with layout (1, 3, 224, 224).
  • The ndarray buffer is passed to ONNX Runtime via ort::Value::from_array, eliminating memory copies.
  • Predictable Latency: Free from garbage collection pauses and interpreter lock contention. Under high load, Rust maintains flat p99 tail latency.

docs.title: 5. Preprocessing & Numerical Parity (Eliminating Train-Serve Skew)
docs.text:
A critical failure mode in production Computer Vision is Train-Serve Skew: subtle mathematical discrepancies between training transforms and serving inference (e.g., resizing algorithm differences, color channel ordering, rounding errors, normalization constants).

RecycleNet-K8s prevents Train-Serve Skew by standardizing preprocessing mathematically across Python and Rust:

docs.title: Mathematical Transformation Pipeline
docs.text:
$$\text{Raw Bytes} \xrightarrow{\text{Decode}} \mathbf{I}{\text{RGB}} \xrightarrow{\text{Scale}} [0.0, 1.0] \xrightarrow{\text{Resize}} 224 \times 224 \xrightarrow{\text{Normalize}} \mathbf{T}{(1, 3, 224, 224)}$$

  1. Color Conversion: Raw compressed byte stream is converted to standard 8-bit RGB (eliminating alpha channels and grayscale variance).
  2. Floating-Point Scaling: Integer pixel values $p \in [0, 255]$ are scaled to single-precision float $v = \frac{p}{255.0}$.
  3. Spatial Resizing: Resized to exactly $224 \times 224$ pixels using standard Bilinear Interpolation (torchvision.transforms.v2.Resize and image::imageops::FilterType::Triangle).
  4. Channel Normalization: $$x_{c, i, j}^{\text{norm}} = \frac{x_{c, i, j} - \mu_c}{\sigma_c}$$ Where ImageNet standard constants are strictly enforced: $$\mu = [0.485, 0.456, 0.406], \quad \sigma = [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]$$
  5. Memory Layout Transformation:
  6. Python: Handled via PyTorch's native NCHW tensor layout.
  7. Rust: Transforms row-major interleaved HWC pixel buffers into contiguous planar NCHW via ndarray::Array4<f32>::zeros((1, 3, 224, 224)).

docs.title: Automated Numerical Parity Gate
docs.text: Automated test suites (benchmarks/benchmark_suite.py and tests/test_rust_parity.py) enforce strict parity criteria across synthetic and real TrashNet test images: - Top-1 Class Agreement: Must equal 100.0%. - Maximum Softmax Probability Difference ($\Delta_\max$): $$\Delta_\max = \max_{i \in \text{classes}} |P_{\text{Python}}(c_i) - P_{\text{Rust}}(c_i)| \le 1.0 \times 10^{-3}$$ - Any discrepancy exceeding $10^{-3}$ immediately fails CI/CD, guaranteeing zero Train-Serve Skew in production.

def extract_dataset(self) -> Path:
    """Extract the zipped dataset archive into the raw output directory.

    Returns:
        Path: Path to the extracted dataset directory containing class subfolders.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the zip archive does not exist at `zip_source`.
        zipfile.BadZipFile: If the file is not a valid zip archive.
    """
    output_dir = Path(self.config.raw_output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(self.config.zip_source, "r") as zip_file:
        for member in zip_file.infolist():
            filename = member.filename
            # Skip macOS metadata folders and AppleDouble / hidden files
            if (
                filename.startswith("__MACOSX")
                or "/__MACOSX" in filename
                or Path(filename).name.startswith("._")
                or Path(filename).name == ".DS_Store"
            ):
                continue
            zip_file.extract(member, output_dir)
    # Dynamically detect if dataset was extracted into a single wrapper directory
    subdirs = [
        p
        for p in output_dir.iterdir()
        if p.is_dir() and not p.name.startswith(".") and p.name != "__MACOSX"
    ]
    if len(subdirs) == 1 and any(p.is_dir() for p in subdirs[0].iterdir()):
        return subdirs[0]
    return output_dir

def get_dataloaders(
    self,
    raw_data_dir: Path,
) -> tuple[DataLoader[SampleType], DataLoader[SampleType], DataLoader[SampleType]]:
    """Build and return DataLoaders for train, validation, and test partitions.

    Discovers dataset classes, generates reproducible splits, binds transformations,
    and constructs corresponding DataLoaders.

    Args:
        raw_data_dir: Path to directory containing class subfolders of images.

    Returns:
        tuple[
            DataLoader[SampleType],
            DataLoader[SampleType],
            DataLoader[SampleType]
        ]:
            Train, validation, and test DataLoaders.
    """

    full_dataset = datasets.ImageFolder(root=raw_data_dir)
    self.classes = full_dataset.classes
    self.class_to_idx = full_dataset.class_to_idx

    train_transform, valid_transform = self._get_transformations()

    split_generator = self._get_generator()
    train_sub, valid_sub, test_sub = random_split(
        full_dataset,
        (
            self.config.train_split,
            self.config.eval_split,
            self.config.test_split,
        ),
        generator=split_generator,
    )

    train_idx_set = set(train_sub.indices)
    valid_idx_set = set(valid_sub.indices)
    test_idx_set = set(test_sub.indices)
    zero_overlap = (
        train_idx_set.isdisjoint(valid_idx_set)
        and train_idx_set.isdisjoint(test_idx_set)
        and valid_idx_set.isdisjoint(test_idx_set)
    )
    if not zero_overlap:
        raise ValueError(
            "Data leakage detected: overlapping indices across splits."
        )

    targets_arr = np.asarray(full_dataset.targets)
    split_map = {
        "train": train_sub.indices,
        "validation": valid_sub.indices,
        "test": test_sub.indices,
    }
    partitions_summary: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for split_name, indices in split_map.items():
        split_targets = targets_arr[indices]
        total_split = len(indices)
        class_counts: dict[str, dict[str, int | float]] = {}
        for cls_idx, cls_name in enumerate(self.classes):
            count = int(np.sum(split_targets == cls_idx))
            pct = (
                round((count / total_split * 100.0), 2) if total_split > 0 else 0.0
            )
            class_counts[cls_name] = {"count": count, "percentage": pct}
        partitions_summary[split_name] = {
            "total_samples": total_split,
            "classes": class_counts,
        }
    self.split_distribution = {
        "total_samples": len(full_dataset),
        "zero_overlap_verified": zero_overlap,
        "partitions": partitions_summary,
    }

    train_ds = RecycleDataset(train_sub, train_transform)
    valid_ds = RecycleDataset(valid_sub, valid_transform)
    test_ds = RecycleDataset(test_sub, valid_transform)

    train_loader = self._build_dataloader(train_ds, True)
    valid_loader = self._build_dataloader(valid_ds, False)
    test_loader = self._build_dataloader(test_ds, False)

    return train_loader, valid_loader, test_loader

def build_mobilenet_v3(
    num_classes: int,
    freeze_base: bool = True,
    size: MobileNetV3Size = "small",
) -> MobileNetV3:
    """Construct a pre-trained MobileNetV3 architecture for classification.

    Loads the default ImageNet pre-trained weights for the requested size,
    freezes backbone convolutional layers if requested, and replaces the final
    linear layer with a new trainable head matching `num_classes`.

    Args:
        num_classes: Number of target output classes (e.g., 6 for TrashNet).
        freeze_base: Whether to freeze feature extractor weights for transfer learning.
        size: MobileNetV3 variant to build, either 'small' or 'large'.

    Returns:
        MobileNetV3: Configured PyTorch neural network model.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If `size` is not a supported MobileNetV3 variant.

    Example:
        ```python
        from src.components.model import build_mobilenet_v3

        model = build_mobilenet_v3(num_classes=6, freeze_base=True, size="large")
        ```
    """
    if size == "small":
        model = mobilenet_v3_small(weights=MobileNet_V3_Small_Weights.DEFAULT)
    elif size == "large":
        model = mobilenet_v3_large(weights=MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights.DEFAULT)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported MobileNetV3 size '{size}'. "
            f"Expected one of {SUPPORTED_MOBILENET_V3_SIZES}."
        )

    if freeze_base:
        for param in model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False

    # replace the last layer
    last_in_features: int = model.classifier[-1].in_features  # type: ignore
    model.classifier[-1] = nn.Linear(
        in_features=last_in_features,
        out_features=num_classes,
        bias=True,
    )

    # ensure that new last layer is trainable
    for param in model.classifier[-1].parameters():
        param.requires_grad = True
    return model

def get_scheduler(
    optimizer: Optimizer,
    scheduler_type: str = "cosine",
    epochs: int = 10,
    min_lr: float = 1e-5,
    warmup_epochs: int = 0,
    patience: int = 2,
    factor: float = 0.5,
) -> LRScheduler | ReduceLROnPlateau | None:
    """Instantiate and return the configured learning rate scheduler.

    Args:
        optimizer: Optimizer instance whose learning rate will be scheduled.
        scheduler_type: Type of scheduler ('cosine', 'plateau', or 'none').
        epochs: Total number of training epochs (used for CosineAnnealingLR).
        min_lr: Minimum learning rate threshold.
        warmup_epochs: Number of linear warmup epochs (applicable to cosine).
        patience: Epoch patience for ReduceLROnPlateau before decaying LR.
        factor: Decay multiplicative factor for ReduceLROnPlateau.

    Returns:
        Configured LRScheduler, ReduceLROnPlateau, or None if disabled.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If an unsupported scheduler_type is provided.
    """
    scheduler_type_norm = (scheduler_type or "").strip().lower()

    if scheduler_type_norm in ("none", ""):
        return None

    if scheduler_type_norm == "cosine":
        if warmup_epochs > 0 and epochs > warmup_epochs:
            warmup = LinearLR(
                optimizer,
                start_factor=0.1,
                end_factor=1.0,
                total_iters=warmup_epochs,
            )
            cosine = CosineAnnealingLR(
                optimizer,
                T_max=epochs - warmup_epochs,
                eta_min=min_lr,
            )
            return SequentialLR(
                optimizer,
                schedulers=[warmup, cosine],
                milestones=[warmup_epochs],
            )
        return CosineAnnealingLR(
            optimizer,
            T_max=max(epochs, 1),
            eta_min=min_lr,
        )

    if scheduler_type_norm == "plateau":
        return ReduceLROnPlateau(
            optimizer,
            mode="min",
            factor=factor,
            patience=patience,
            min_lr=min_lr,
        )

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported scheduler type '{scheduler_type}'. "
        "Allowed options are: 'cosine', 'plateau', 'none'."
    )

def calculate_roc_auc(
    y_true: np.ndarray,
    y_score: np.ndarray,
) -> float:
    """Compute macro-averaged One-vs-Rest (OvR) ROC AUC score.

            and f1_score.

        return {

            "precision": 0.0,
            "recall": 0.0,
            "f1_score": 0.0,

    )
    metrics["recall"] = float(

    )
    metrics["f1_score"] = float(
        f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average=AVERAGE, zero_division=0)
    )
    return metrics

def run(self) -> None:
    """Execute the distributed training, logging, and evaluation workflow.

    Raises:
        RecycleNetException: If an error occurs during distributed training
            or registration.
    """
    logger.info("Starting distributed training pipeline...")

    try:
        effective_device, resources = assign_ray_resources(
            self.config.training.device,
            self.config.training.cpu_resources_per_worker,
            self.config.training.gpu_resources_per_worker,
        )
        use_gpu = effective_device == "cuda"

        scaling_config = ScalingConfig(
            num_workers=self.config.training.num_workers,
            use_gpu=use_gpu,
            resources_per_worker=resources,
        )

        checkpoint_config = CheckpointConfig(
            num_to_keep=1,
            checkpoint_score_attribute="valid_loss",
            checkpoint_score_order="min",
        )

        failure_config = FailureConfig(
            max_failures=0,
        )

        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
        run_name = f"{self.config.tracking.experiment_name}_{timestamp}"

        run_config = RunConfig(
            name=run_name,
            checkpoint_config=checkpoint_config,
            failure_config=failure_config,
        )

        dataset_dir = self.ingestion.extract_dataset().resolve()
        logger.info("Dataset extracted at: %s", dataset_dir)

        self.transformation.discover_classes(dataset_dir)
        num_classes = len(self.transformation.classes)
        logger.info(

            "learning_rate": self.config.training.learning_rate,
            "weight_decay": self.config.training.weight_decay,
            "epochs": self.config.training.epochs,

            "model_size": self.config.model.size,
            "tracking_uri": resolve_tracking_uri(self.config.tracking.tracking_uri),
        }

        split_dist: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        try:
            split_dist = self.transformation.get_split_distribution(dataset_dir)
        except Exception as split_exc:
            logger.debug("Split distribution computation skipped: %s", split_exc)

        self.logmodel.set_experiment_tracking()
        pipeline_tags = self.config.tracking.tags.copy()
        pipeline_tags["hardware"] = effective_device

        with self.logmodel.start_run() as active_run:
            logger.info("Active MLflow Run ID: %s", active_run.info.run_id)

            # Inject the active run_id so workers can log in real-time to this run
            train_loop_config["mlflow_run_id"] = active_run.info.run_id

            trainer = TorchTrainer(
                train_loop_per_worker=train_loop_per_worker,
                train_loop_config=train_loop_config,
                scaling_config=scaling_config,
                run_config=run_config,
            )

            idx_to_class = {
                str(idx): name
                for idx, name in enumerate(self.transformation.classes)
            }

            self.logmodel.log_pipeline_metadata(
                idx_to_class=idx_to_class,
                tags=pipeline_tags,
                params={
                    "epochs": self.config.training.epochs,
                    "patience": self.config.training.patience,
                    "batch_size": self.config.transformation.batch_size,
                    "learning_rate": self.config.training.learning_rate,
                    "weight_decay": self.config.training.weight_decay,
                    "scheduler": self.config.training.scheduler,
                    "min_lr": self.config.training.min_lr,
                    "warmup_epochs": self.config.training.warmup_epochs,
                    "num_workers": self.config.training.num_workers,
                },
                config_dict=self.config.model_dump(mode="json"),
                split_distribution=split_dist,
            )

            logger.info("Running Ray distributed training...")
            results = trainer.fit()

            best_checkpoint = results.checkpoint
            if best_checkpoint is None:
                raise RecycleNetException(
                    "Ray training completed without generating a valid checkpoint."
                )

            # Epoch and test metrics are logged by the rank-0 worker, because
            # Ray Train v2 only keeps metrics of checkpointed reports.

            logger.info("Restoring best model checkpoint for model registry...")
            best_model = build_mobilenet_v3(
                num_classes, size=self.config.model.size
            )
            with best_checkpoint.as_directory() as checkpoint_dir:
                checkpoint_path = os.path.join(checkpoint_dir, "model.pt")
                checkpoint_data = torch.load(
                    checkpoint_path,
                    map_location="cpu",
                    weights_only=True,
                )
                best_model.load_state_dict(checkpoint_data["model_state"])

            logger.info("Registering model in MLflow Model Registry...")
            sample_shape = (
                1,
                3,
                *self.config.transformation.image_size,
            )
            self.logmodel.register_checkpoint(
                model=best_model,
                input_shape=sample_shape,
            )
            logger.info("Pipeline successfully completed.")

    except Exception as e:
        raise RecycleNetException(
            "Failure during the distributed training or assessment cycle", e
        ) from e

def train_loop_per_worker(
    config: dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    """Execute the distributed training and validation loop for a single Ray worker.

    Args:
        config: Dictionary containing dataset paths, hyperparameters, and settings.
    """
    try:
        make_reproducibility(config["reproducibility"])
        worker_device = ray.train.torch.get_device()

        transformation = DataTransformation(
            config["transformation"],
            seed=config["reproducibility"].torch_seed,
        )
        train_loader, valid_loader, test_loader = transformation.get_dataloaders(
            config["raw_path"]
        )
        train_loader = ray.train.torch.prepare_data_loader(train_loader)

        model = build_mobilenet_v3(
            len(transformation.classes), size=config.get("model_size", "small")
        )
        model = ray.train.torch.prepare_model(model)

        criterion = get_criterion()
        optimizer = get_optimizer(
            filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, model.parameters()),
            learning_rate=config["learning_rate"],
            weight_decay=config["weight_decay"],
        )
        scheduler = get_scheduler(
            optimizer,
            scheduler_type=config.get("scheduler", "cosine"),
            epochs=config["epochs"],
            min_lr=config.get("min_lr", 1e-5),
            warmup_epochs=config.get("warmup_epochs", 0),
            patience=max(1, config.get("patience", 5) // 2),
        )

        trainer = TrainStep(
            model=model,
            train_loader=train_loader,
            val_loader=valid_loader,
            criterion=criterion,
            optimizer=optimizer,
            device=worker_device,
        )

        best_vloss = float("inf")
        best_model_weights = None
        history: list[dict[str, float]] = []
        patience_counter = 0
        patience = config.get("patience", 5)

        try:
            world_rank = ray.train.get_context().get_world_rank()
        except RuntimeError:
            world_rank = 0

        for epoch in range(config["epochs"]):
            sampler = getattr(train_loader, "sampler", None)
            if sampler and hasattr(sampler, "set_epoch"):
                sampler.set_epoch(epoch)

            metrics = trainer.train_valid_step()
            current_lr = float(optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"])
            metrics["learning_rate"] = current_lr

            if scheduler is not None:
                if isinstance(scheduler, ReduceLROnPlateau):
                    scheduler.step(metrics["valid_loss"])
                else:
                    scheduler.step()

            epoch_record: dict[str, float] = {
                "train_loss": float(metrics["train_loss"]),
                "valid_loss": float(metrics["valid_loss"]),
                "valid_accuracy": float(metrics.get("valid_accuracy", 0.0)),
                "valid_precision": float(metrics.get("valid_precision", 0.0)),
                "valid_recall": float(metrics.get("valid_recall", 0.0)),
                "valid_f1_score": float(metrics.get("valid_f1_score", 0.0)),
                "learning_rate": current_lr,
            }
            history.append(epoch_record)

            logger.info(
                "Epoch [%d/%d] - train_loss: %.4f - valid_loss: %.4f - "
                "valid_accuracy: %.4f - valid_f1: %.4f",
                epoch + 1,
                config["epochs"],
                epoch_record["train_loss"],
                epoch_record["valid_loss"],
                epoch_record["valid_accuracy"],
                epoch_record["valid_f1_score"],
            )

            # --- Real-time MLflow logging (rank 0 only to avoid concurrent writes) ---
            mlflow_run_id = config.get("mlflow_run_id")
            tracking_uri = config.get("tracking_uri")
            if world_rank == 0 and mlflow_run_id and tracking_uri:
                try:
                    client = MlflowClient(tracking_uri=tracking_uri)
                    for key, value in epoch_record.items():
                        client.log_metric(
                            run_id=mlflow_run_id,
                            key=key,
                            value=value,
                            step=epoch,
                        )
                except Exception as exc:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Real-time MLflow worker metric logging failed: %s", exc
                    )

            # --- Early stopping check ---
            if metrics["valid_loss"] < best_vloss:
                best_vloss = metrics["valid_loss"]
                patience_counter = 0
                raw_model = (
                    model.module
                    if isinstance(model, DistributedDataParallel)
                    else model
                )
                best_model_weights = {
                    k: v.cpu().clone() for k, v in raw_model.state_dict().items()
                }
            else:
                patience_counter += 1

            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_checkpoint_dir:
                raw_model = (
                    model.module
                    if isinstance(model, DistributedDataParallel)
                    else model
                )
                state_dict = raw_model.state_dict()
                torch.save(
                    {
                        "epoch": epoch,
                        "model_state": state_dict,
                        "optimizer_state": optimizer.state_dict(),
                    },
                    os.path.join(temp_checkpoint_dir, "model.pt"),
                )

                ray.train.report(
                    metrics=metrics,
                    checkpoint=Checkpoint.from_directory(temp_checkpoint_dir),
                )

            if patience_counter >= patience:
                logger.info(
                    "Early stopping triggered at epoch %d (patience=%d)",
                    epoch + 1,
                    patience,
                )
                break

        if best_model_weights is not None:
            raw_model = (
                model.module if isinstance(model, DistributedDataParallel) else model
            )
            raw_model.load_state_dict(best_model_weights)

        test_loader = ray.train.torch.prepare_data_loader(test_loader)
        test_distributed = TestDistributed(
            model=model,
            test_loader=test_loader,
            criterion=criterion,
            num_classes=len(transformation.classes),
            classes_name=transformation.classes,
            device=worker_device,
        )
        eval_metrics = test_distributed.compute_distributed_test_metrics()

        if (
            world_rank == 0
            and config.get("mlflow_run_id")
            and config.get("tracking_uri")
        ):
            try:
                _log_test_metrics_to_mlflow(
                    MlflowClient(tracking_uri=config["tracking_uri"]),
                    config["mlflow_run_id"],
                    eval_metrics,
                )
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.warning("Worker MLflow test metric logging failed: %s", exc)

        eval_metrics["history"] = history
        ray.train.report(eval_metrics)

    finally:
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        gc.collect()

def run(self) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, dict[str, Any] | None]:
    """Execute the Ray Tune HPO search across configured worker resources.

    Returns:
        tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, dict[str, Any] | None]: Best trial
            hyperparameter configuration dictionary and evaluation metrics.

    Raises:
        RecycleNetException: If Ray Tune encounters an unrecoverable failure.
    """
    logger.info("Initializing Ray Tune HPO pipeline...")

    try:
        device, resources = assign_ray_resources(
            self.config.hpo.device,
            self.config.hpo.cpu_resources_per_trial,
            self.config.hpo.gpu_resources_per_trial,
        )

        logger.info(
            "HPO hardware resolved: effective_device=%s, "
            "cpu_per_trial=%s, gpu_per_trial=%s",
            device,
            resources.get("CPU", 0.0),
            resources.get("GPU", 0.0),
        )

        param_space = {
            "learning_rate": tune.loguniform(
                self.config.hpo.learning_rate_range[0],
                self.config.hpo.learning_rate_range[1],
            ),
            "weight_decay": tune.loguniform(
                self.config.hpo.weight_decay_range[0],
                self.config.hpo.weight_decay_range[1],
            ),
            "batch_size": tune.choice(self.config.hpo.batch_size),
            "max_epochs": self.config.hpo.max_epochs,
            "grace_period": self.config.hpo.grace_period,
            "dataloader_n_workers": self.config.hpo.dataloader_n_workers,
            "device": device,
        }

        dataset_dir = self.ingestion.extract_dataset().resolve()
        logger.info("Dataset extracted at: %s", dataset_dir)

        tuner_parameters = tune.with_parameters(
            train_eval_trial,
            data_dir=dataset_dir,
            app_config=self.config,
        )

        tuner_resources = tune.with_resources(
            tuner_parameters,
            resources=resources,
        )

        scheduler = ASHAScheduler(
            max_t=self.config.hpo.max_epochs,
            grace_period=self.config.hpo.grace_period,
            reduction_factor=self.config.hpo.reduction_factor,
            metric="valid_loss",
            mode="min",
        )

        search_alg = OptunaSearch(
            metric="valid_loss",
            mode="min",
        )

        tune_config = tune.TuneConfig(
            scheduler=scheduler,
            search_alg=search_alg,
            num_samples=self.config.hpo.num_samples,
            max_concurrent_trials=self.config.hpo.max_concurrent_trials,
        )

        run_config = tune.RunConfig(
            name=self.config.hpo.experiment_name,
            failure_config=FailureConfig(
                max_failures=0,
                fail_fast=True,
            ),
            callbacks=[
                MLflowLoggerCallback(
                    tracking_uri=self.config.tracking.tracking_uri,
                    experiment_name=self.config.hpo.experiment_name,
                    save_artifact=True,
                )
            ],
        )

        tuner = tune.Tuner(
            trainable=tuner_resources,
            param_space=param_space,
            tune_config=tune_config,
            run_config=run_config,
        )

        logger.info(
            "Starting Ray Tune execution (samples=%d, max_concurrent=%d)...",
            self.config.hpo.num_samples,
            self.config.hpo.max_concurrent_trials,
        )

        results = tuner.fit()

        if results.errors:
            logger.error(
                "Ray Tune HPO aborted: detected %d trial(s) with errors.",
                results.num_errors,
            )

            for error in results.errors:
                root_cause = getattr(error, "cause", error)
                err_type = type(root_cause).__name__
                err_msg = str(root_cause)

                tb_lines = str(error).strip().splitlines()
                tail_tb = "\n    ".join(tb_lines[-8:])

                logger.error(
                    "Trial failed with %s: %s\n"
                    "  Traceback snippet (last lines):\n    %s",
                    err_type,
                    err_msg,
                    tail_tb,
                )

            raise RecycleNetException(
                f"Ray Tune HPO aborted due to failures in "
                f"{len(results.errors)} trial(s)."
            )

        best_result = results.get_best_result(metric="valid_loss", mode="min")
        if best_result is None or best_result.config is None:
            raise RecycleNetException(
                "Ray Tune completed without finding a valid best result."
            )

        logger.info("Ray Tune HPO search completed successfully.")
        logger.info("Best trial config: %s", best_result.config)
        logger.info("Best trial metrics: %s", best_result.metrics)

        best_config = best_result.config
        best_metrics: dict[str, Any] = best_result.metrics or {}

        output_config: dict[str, Any] = {
            "ingestion": {
                "zip_source": str(self.config.ingestion.zip_source),
                "raw_output_dir": str(self.config.ingestion.raw_output_dir),
            },
            "transformation": {
                "image_size": list(self.config.transformation.image_size),
                "image_mean": list(self.config.transformation.image_mean),
                "image_std": list(self.config.transformation.image_std),
                "random_h_flip": self.config.transformation.random_h_flip,
                "random_rotation": (
                    list(self.config.transformation.random_rotation)
                    if isinstance(self.config.transformation.random_rotation, tuple)
                    else self.config.transformation.random_rotation
                ),
                "train_split": self.config.transformation.train_split,
                "eval_split": self.config.transformation.eval_split,
                "test_split": self.config.transformation.test_split,
                "batch_size": int(
                    best_config.get(
                        "batch_size", self.config.transformation.batch_size
                    )
                ),
                "num_workers": int(
                    best_config.get(
                        "dataloader_n_workers",
                        self.config.transformation.num_workers,
                    )
                ),
                "pin_memory": self.config.transformation.pin_memory,
            },
            "reproducibility": {
                "random_seed": self.config.reproducibility.random_seed,
                "numpy_seed": self.config.reproducibility.numpy_seed,
                "torch_seed": self.config.reproducibility.torch_seed,
                "deterministic": self.config.reproducibility.deterministic,
                "warn_only": self.config.reproducibility.warn_only,
            },
            "training": {
                "epochs": self.config.training.epochs,
                "patience": self.config.training.patience,
                "learning_rate": float(
                    best_config.get(
                        "learning_rate", self.config.training.learning_rate
                    )
                ),
                "weight_decay": float(
                    best_config.get(
                        "weight_decay", self.config.training.weight_decay
                    )
                ),
                "scheduler": self.config.training.scheduler,
                "min_lr": self.config.training.min_lr,
                "warmup_epochs": self.config.training.warmup_epochs,
                "num_workers": self.config.training.num_workers,
                "cpu_resources_per_worker": (
                    self.config.training.cpu_resources_per_worker
                ),
                "gpu_resources_per_worker": (
                    self.config.training.gpu_resources_per_worker
                ),
                "device": self.config.training.device,
            },
            "model": {
                "size": self.config.model.size,
            },
            "tracking": {
                "experiment_name": self.config.tracking.experiment_name,
                "registered_model_name": self.config.tracking.registered_model_name,
                "tracking_uri": resolve_tracking_uri(
                    self.config.tracking.tracking_uri
                ),
                "tags": dict(self.config.tracking.tags),
            },
            "hpo": {
                "weight_decay_range": list(self.config.hpo.weight_decay_range),
                "learning_rate_range": list(self.config.hpo.learning_rate_range),
                "batch_size": self.config.hpo.batch_size,
                "num_samples": self.config.hpo.num_samples,
                "max_epochs": self.config.hpo.max_epochs,
                "grace_period": self.config.hpo.grace_period,
                "reduction_factor": self.config.hpo.reduction_factor,
                "dataloader_n_workers": self.config.hpo.dataloader_n_workers,
                "max_concurrent_trials": self.config.hpo.max_concurrent_trials,
                "cpu_resources_per_trial": self.config.hpo.cpu_resources_per_trial,
                "gpu_resources_per_trial": self.config.hpo.gpu_resources_per_trial,
                "device": self.config.hpo.device,
                "experiment_name": self.config.hpo.experiment_name,
                "best_config_path": str(self.config.hpo.best_config_path),
            },
        }

        output_path = Path(self.config.hpo.best_config_path)
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            yaml.dump(
                output_config, f, default_flow_style=False, allow_unicode=True
            )

        logger.info(
            "Best HPO config saved to %s | lr=%.6f, wd=%.6f, batch=%d",
            output_path,
            output_config["training"]["learning_rate"],
            output_config["training"]["weight_decay"],
            output_config["transformation"]["batch_size"],
        )
        logger.info("Best HPO metrics: %s", best_metrics)

        return best_result.config, best_result.metrics

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Critical error during HPO pipeline execution: %s", str(e))
        raise RecycleNetException(
            "Error encountered during distributed Ray Tune HPO execution", e
        ) from e

def train_eval_trial(

def assign_ray_resources(
    requested_device: str,
    cpu_resources: float,
    gpu_resources: float,
) -> tuple[str, dict[str, float]]:
    """Dynamically resolve Ray resource allocations based on hardware availability.

    Args:
        requested_device: User-configured device preference ('auto', 'cuda', or 'cpu').
        cpu_resources: Number of CPU cores requested per trial.
        gpu_resources: Fractional or integer GPUs requested per trial.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, dict[str, float]]: Effective compute device ('cuda' or 'cpu') and
            sanitized resource mapping for Ray Tune.
    """
    has_cuda = is_available()
    requested_device = requested_device.lower()

    if requested_device == "auto":
        effective_device = "cuda" if has_cuda else "cpu"
    elif requested_device == "cuda" and not has_cuda:
        logger.warning(
            "CUDA requested in config but not available. Falling back to CPU."
        )
        effective_device = "cpu"
    else:
        effective_device = requested_device

    use_gpu = effective_device == "cuda"
    resources: dict[str, float] = {"CPU": float(cpu_resources)}
    if use_gpu and gpu_resources > 0:
        resources["GPU"] = float(gpu_resources)
    return effective_device, resources

def make_reproducibility(config: ReproducibilityConfig) -> None:
    """Set random seeds across Python, NumPy, PyTorch, and CUDA backends.

    Args:
        config: Configuration containing random seed values.
    """
    os.environ["PYTHONHASHSEED"] = str(config.random_seed)
    random.seed(config.random_seed)
    np.random.seed(config.numpy_seed)
    torch.manual_seed(config.torch_seed)

    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed(config.torch_seed)
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(config.torch_seed)

        if config.deterministic:
            os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"] = ":4096:8"
            torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
            torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
        else:
            torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = False
            torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True

    if config.deterministic:
        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=config.warn_only)
        logger.info("Strict deterministic mode activated (bitwise reproducibility).")
    else:
        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(False)
        logger.info(
            "High-throughput training mode activated (statistical reproducibility)."
        )

def seed_worker(_worker_id: int) -> None:
    """Set random seeds for NumPy and Python random in DataLoader worker processes.

    loading workers by reseeding external libraries using PyTorch's generated

def get_logger(name: str, level: int | None = None) -> logging.Logger:
    """Create or retrieve a configured logger instance.

    Configures a `StreamHandler` targeting `sys.stdout` with either `JSONFormatter`
    or `LocalFormatter` depending on the runtime environment.

    Args:
        name: The name of the logger, typically `__name__` of the calling module.
        level: Optional logging level. If None, defaults to the `LOG_LEVEL`
            environment variable or `logging.INFO`.

    Returns:
        logging.Logger: Configured logger instance ready for logging.
    """
    logger = logging.getLogger(name)

    # if it already configured
    if logger.handlers:
        return logger

    # set level to INFO is it's been set
    if level is None:
        level = getattr(
            logging, os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO").upper(), logging.INFO
        )

    logger.setLevel(level)  # type: ignore

    logger.propagate = False

    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
    handler.setFormatter(JSONFormatter() if _use_json_logging() else LocalFormatter())
    logger.addHandler(handler)

    return logger

def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
    """Formats the specified LogRecord as a single-line JSON payload.

    Args:
        record: The LogRecord instance to format.

    Returns:
        str: JSON-encoded string representation of the log record.
    """
    payload = {
        "severity": _LEVEL_TO_GCP_SEVERITY.get(record.levelno, "DEFAULT"),
        "message": record.getMessage(),
        "logger": record.name,
        "timestamp": datetime.fromtimestamp(record.created, tz=UTC).isoformat(),
    }

    if record.exc_info:
        payload["exception"] = self.formatException(record.exc_info)

    # merge in anything passed via extra={...} as structured field
    for key, value in record.__dict__.items():
        if key in _RESERVED_RECORD_KEYS or key in payload:
            continue

        payload[key] = value

    try:
        return json.dumps(payload, default=str)
    except TypeError, ValueError:
        sanitized = {k: str(v) for k, v in payload.items()}
        return json.dumps(sanitized)

def __init__(self, datefmt: str = "%H:%M:%S") -> None:
    """Initializes the LocalFormatter with per-level ANSI color formatters.

    Args:
        datefmt: Format string for the timestamp in log messages.
    """
    super().__init__(datefmt=datefmt)

    self._formatters = {
        level: logging.Formatter(
            f"{color}%(asctime)s | %(levelname)-8s | "
            f"%(name)s | %(message)s{self.RESET}",
            datefmt=datefmt,
        )
        for level, color in self.COLORS.items()
    }
    self._default = logging.Formatter(
        "%(asctime)s | %(levelname)-8s | %(name)s | %(message)s",
        datefmt=datefmt,
    )

def __init__(
    self,
    message: str,
    original_error: BaseException | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize RecycleNetException with detailed error and traceback metadata.

    Args:
        message: High-level explanation of what failed.
        original_error: The original caught exception to chain and extract
            context from.
    """
    self.message: str = message
    self.original_error: BaseException | None = original_error

    if original_error is not None:
        tb = original_error.__traceback__
        extracted = traceback.extract_tb(tb)
        if extracted:
            last_frame = extracted[-1]
            formatted = (
                f"{message} | Cause: [{type(original_error).__name__}: "
                f"{original_error}] "
                f"in {last_frame.filename}, line {last_frame.lineno} "
                f"({last_frame.name})"
            )
        else:
            formatted = (
                f"{message} | Cause: [{type(original_error).__name__}: "
                f"{original_error}]"
            )
    else:
        formatted = message

    super().__init__(formatted)
    if original_error is not None:
        self.__cause__ = original_error
